APPROVE
`JudgeAsync` now scores about 11 (each early-return branch moved into `ShellStop`, `CheckCorpusPinAsync`, `EngineTestsStopAsync` or `MeasureBenchAsync` costs only one `if`). The checks still run in the same order with the same outcomes, reasons, suite, delta, units, items, corpus pin and side gains on every path. I see nothing that should break the build, though I did not compile it, and that assumes `ChangedFilesAsync` returns a type that converts to `IReadOnlyList<string>`.
